title: Suppressing Majorana Hybridization in Atomically Assembled Cr Chains on β-Bi2Pd
why_careful: Both ends of the same chain measured along a controlled length series (Cr4 to Cr12) with gap closing and reopening, chains built in defect-free regions, a pristine-surface reference spectrum for the gap estimate, microwave-assisted tunnelling, and a model test of the end-to-end asymmetry.

spans: This imbalance is confined to the end regions. The
central part of the chain remains comparatively weakly
affected, suggesting that the asymmetry originates from
a local or slowly varying microscopic perturbation that
modifies the spatial distribution of the end-mode spec-
tral weight without removing the zero-energy state [31].
To test this possibility, we introduce a variation of 6%
between one end atom and the central atom in their re-
spective Kondo exchange interactions with the substrate,
keeping the other half of the chain unperturbed. The re-
sulting calculated LDOS [Fig. 4(d)] reproduces the ob-
served distortion of the end-state profile. Thus, a small
variation of the local coupling to the superconducting
substrate is sufficient to account for the measured asym-
metry while preserving the zero-energy character of the
end state [18, 31].
